A1.justification: Both complete 30-page PDFs describe the same PLaCy research. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including the rotated tables and relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original OU/dOU simulations, nonlinear-system experiments, and evaluations on Rivers and AirQuality, including F1, TNR and execution-time results.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds negative-control and acyclicity experiments in Appendices E.6–E.7 and Tables 13–15.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1's spectral fitting and Granger-testing pipeline remains unchanged. Appendix E.7 adds an evaluated postprocessing variant that iteratively removes highest-p-value edges until the recovered graph is acyclic.

E1.justification: The OU/dOU scenarios, nonlinear-system test, Rivers and AirQuality remain the same. The new controls reuse existing dataset coverage; the nonlinear experiment already appeared in v2 Appendix D.4.1.

E2.justification: v3 adds the Petersen negative-control comparator in Table 13 and its true-edge-count variant in Table 14. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations compare controls based on predicted versus true edge counts and test acyclic postprocessing under specified synthetic settings. Existing data generation, F1/TNR metrics, window length 50, stride 1 and 10-lag settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 13–14 add targeted checks against chance-level reconstruction, including an edge-count control. Table 15 tests the effect of enforcing acyclicity. Existing window/stride sensitivity, nonlinear-system and spectral-PCMCI analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces significance assessment against Petersen negative controls and explicitly identifies Table 13's uncertainty as standard deviation. The existing policy of 100 runs, except 10 seeds for Rhino, remains unchanged; no increase in those run counts is documented.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, figure and runtime results remain unchanged. Tables 13–15 add results: Table 15 reports F1 0.90 versus 0.77 for acyclic versus standard PLaCy in its N=5 multiplicative-noise OU case. New Table 13 reports Rivers TNR 0.68±0.16, while retained Table 2 reports 0.75±0.13, without explaining the difference.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and the causal-preservation theorem are restricted to linear processes, with amplitude-expressive mechanisms specified in the proof discussion. v3 deletes v2 Theorems 2 and 4 on Markovianity and stationarity for certain nonstationary processes, removes the non-collinearity argument, and replaces the nonlinear proof claim with empirical discussion. Appendix E.8 adds a computational-complexity derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same headline claims about robust discovery, causal-graph preservation and empirical superiority. The narrower formal theorem does not produce corresponding revisions to these headline claims.

C2.justification: v3 treats nonlinear preservation as empirically suggested rather than proved and qualifies preservation through spectral-amplitude changes. It newly explains that default PLaCy does not enforce acyclicity and interprets the added controls. Existing limitations concerning slowly varying spectra and short series remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices E.6–E.7 document the new controls' edge-count choices and the iterative p-value-based cycle-removal rule. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, measured runtimes and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Petersen's negative-control paper as reference 52 and uses it to contextualize performance against random guessing. References 1–51 and the substantive Related Work section are retained.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited wording changes. The appendix is reorganized: hyperparameters follow the detailed results, PCMCI and nonlinear analyses become separate subsections, and execution times move to the end. This is a bounded reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 13–15 and transposes the execution-time table into rows by method. Retained appendix displays move, with some caption and placement changes. All five figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: Narrower theoretical scope and the added chance-level and acyclicity checks provide a limited improvement in claim calibration and validation. Important issues remain: Theorem 3 still asserts independence preservation after its argument is removed, and Table 13's real-data TNR values differ from unchanged Table 2 without explanation. The revision therefore improves the paper modestly without resolving its theoretical and reporting weaknesses.
